drhp.business: Incorporated in 1974, JSL is an EPC contracting company building power transmission and distribution networks across India and global markets. The Company has three lines of operations — transmission lines, substations and rural electrification — with experience in executing high voltage transmission lines up to 800 kV and substations up to 765 kV, and it also manufactures transmission towers at its Nashik plants and offers tower testing services at its R&D Centre at Ghoti. Its major clients are Adani, Vedanta Group, ReNew Power, Apraava, Torrent and PGCIL.

drhp.expansion: During FY 2025-26 the Company completed its principal capacity expansion: commercial manufacturing operations commenced at the second unit, Nashik Plant–II, in January 2026, adding an annual manufacturing capacity of 36,000 MT. With this commissioning, the combined annual manufacturing capacity of Nashik Plant–I and Nashik Plant–II increased to 72,000 MT. Management states the expansion is expected to strengthen the Company's ability to cater to growing customer demand, improve operational efficiencies and support its long-term growth strategy in the power transmission infrastructure sector, …

risks.note: BRSR material-issues table states: 'The Company recognizes the need to prevent disruptions that could be brought by social, natural or legal issues and to ensure ongoing raw material availability' and that 'The disruption to the supply chain may cause discontinuity or availability of the raw material which may affect the business operations.' No mitigation approach is disclosed ('NA' in the mitigation column).
risks.risk: Sustainable procurement / raw material supply-chain disruption — the only material issue the Company itself classifies as a risk with negative financial implications

risks.note: BRSR reports transmission and distribution / 'Construction, erection and maintenance of power and transmission lines' as 100% of turnover, leaving no diversification cushion if T&D EPC ordering slows.
risks.risk: Single-activity concentration — 100% of turnover comes from one business activity

risks.note: Major clients are listed as Adani, Vedanta Group, ReNew Power, Apraava, Torrent and PGCIL; EPC receivable and order-flow exposure is therefore concentrated in a handful of buyers.
risks.risk: Customer and counterparty concentration in a small set of utilities and developers

risks.note: The Company serves 5 states nationally and 2 countries internationally, and exports contribute just 0.02% of total turnover, despite the MD&A citing international transmission opportunities in Asia, Africa and the Middle East as a growth avenue.
risks.risk: Geographic concentration — narrow domestic footprint and negligible export base

risks.note: The MD&A attributes the sector's growth prospects to favourable government policies, regulatory reforms, Green Energy Corridors and utility investment programmes; a slowdown or reform reversal in these programmes would directly compress the addressable EPC opportunity.
risks.risk: Dependence on government policy, reforms and utility capex cycles for order inflow

risks.note: Management notes projects are 'executed across diverse geographies and challenging site conditions'; the business model depends on commissioning complex EHV/HVDC lines and substations on time and at quality.
risks.risk: Execution and project-delivery risk across diverse geographies and challenging site conditions

risks.note: Permanent-employee turnover was 17.53% in FY 2025-26 (25.45% in FY 2024-25, 25.76% in FY 2023-24); the Company itself states it 'recognizes talent as the primary source of its competitive edge' and is 'aiming at being employer of choice', which it has not yet achieved.

The Company has not undertaken reasonable assurance of the BRSR Core (assurance provider and type both blank); women are 4.22% of total employees, 0% of workers, 16.67% of the Board and 25.00% of KMP.
risks.risk: Unassured ESG disclosure and low workforce diversity

sk.overview: Powerica operates across two industries: (1) India's standby power / diesel-generator (DG set) market, where DG sets, UPS, inverters and battery storage provide backup power during outages/voltage fluctuations across commercial, manufacturing, IT/data-centre, telecom and infrastructure sectors (F&S Report); and (2) India's wind power sector within the broader renewable energy industry, where wind plays a pivotal role in the country's energy transition (CRISIL Report).
